predecessors.name: Sultanate of Malacca
predecessors.text: the remnant realm of the Malacca sultans after 1511 (Bintan, Kampar), which Alauddin Riayat Shah II rebuilt on the Johor River; the infobox lists the Malacca Sultanate as predecessor

successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: the whole of Cliopatria's last Johor shape (mainland Johor); the 1885 British Colonial Empire shape contains all 61 cells of it

successors.name: Riau-Lingga Sultanate
successors.text: Riau and Lingga, the Dutch half of the 1824 partition

successors.name: Pahang (Bendahara state and Sultanate)
successors.text: Pahang, treated as separate from Johor by the 1861 treaty

rulers.name: Ali Jalla Abdul Jalil Shah II

ledger.x: 1528: Alauddin Riayat Shah II founds the Johor Sultanate at Pekan Tua.
1528: the Sumatran shore and Terengganu come with the inheritance of Malacca.
1564: the Acehnese sack Johor Lama and the court moves to Bukit Seluyut.
1570: the court returns to Johor Lama.
1587: the Portuguese sack Johor Lama and the capital moves to Batu Sawar.
1612: a Johor army attacks Pekan, Pahang's capital.
1613: Pahang beats Johor with Brunei's help and keeps its independence until the 1623 union.
1618: the court moves to Lingga; the Pahang page has Raja Bujang fleeing to Lingga in 1617 before the Acehnese.
1623: Pahang and Johor share one ruler.
1640: the court returns to Batu Sawar.
1655: Tungkal rebels against Jambi and passes to Johor.
1667: the war with Jambi opens at sea.
1675: with Batu Sawar sacked by Jambi, the court has no fixed seat until 1688.
1679: Johor wins the war with Jambi, no border moves.
1688: the court settles at Kota Tinggi.
1699: Sultan Mahmud II is assassinated and the Bendahara dynasty takes the throne.
1700: the capital moves to Pancur.
1708: the capital moves to Riau.
1715: the capital returns to Pancur.
1720: the capital returns to Riau.
1722: Terengganu becomes an independent sultanate.
1819: the British take a trading post at Singapore.
1824: the Anglo-Dutch Treaty splits the Johor-Riau empire.
1855: Tengku Ali gives up Johor to Temenggong Ibrahim.
1861: Johor and Pahang are recognised as separate states.
1884: Cliopatria's Johor row ends and its British Colonial Empire shape covers all of Johor from 1885.

wars.name: Acehnese and Portuguese attacks on Johor
wars.outcome: Johor Lama sacked by Aceh (1564) and by the Portuguese (1587); Aceh attacked again in 1613 and 1615.

wars.name: Johor-Pahang war
wars.outcome: Pahang repelled Johor in 1613, with Brunei's help, and stayed independent until the 1623 union.

wars.name: Dutch-Portuguese War: siege of Malacca
wars.outcome: Malacca passed to the Dutch East India Company; the Dutch 'agreed not to seek territories or wage war against Johor'.

wars.name: Johor-Jambi war
wars.outcome: Jambi sacked Batu Sawar on 4 April 1673 and Johor won the war in 1679 (Daeng Mangika fled to Palembang on 17 October 1679); no border moved.

wars.name: Raja Kecil's usurpation
wars.outcome: Raja Kecil of Siak held the Johor throne until 'dethroned by Raja Sulaiman's supporters' with Bugis help in 1722; the Bugis then dominated the sultanate 1760-1784.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line; the Sumatran shore and the Peninsula coast are approximate.

The Singapore Strait line of the 1824 treaty is a treaty line (sharp) between Johor and the Dutch sphere, but only as a sea line; the land frontiers with Pahang (1861 treaty) and Malacca are not surveyed.
